# Golden Hour Unboxed

> A free, all-ages, cross-cultural evening celebrating Black entrepreneurship on the Eastside, held during National Black Business Month. It took place Sunday, August 23, 2026 at Bellevue Botanical Garden (Aaron Education Center), 12001 Main St, Bellevue, WA. Produced by ToyBox Consulting & Management as part of the City of Bellevue's Cross-Cultural Center without Walls. This site is the public record of that evening. Year two is in motion.

## What happened

- **Date:** Sunday, August 23, 2026 — during National Black Business Month
- **Venue:** Bellevue Botanical Garden — Aaron Education Center, 12001 Main St, Bellevue, WA 98005
- **Cost:** Free and open to the public, all ages
- **Attendance:** between 130 and 150 people
- **Tables:** twenty Black-owned business and community organization tables
- **On the record:** proclamations from King County and the City of Bellevue
- **Website:** https://goldenhourunboxed.com/
- **Contact:** katoya@toyboxconsulting.net

## The evening, as it ran

- **Sunset Sounds** — acoustic music, spoken word and movement from cross-cultural artists
- **Commissioned spoken word** — "Keep the Receipts," performed by Melissa Margain
- **Storyteller for the Convening** — Chezik Tsunoda, founder of No More Under, honored with a lapel pin
- **Micro Speed Pitching Showcase** — two-minute pitches from emerging Black entrepreneurs
- **Pack the Box Drive** — school supplies and cash gifts for students in the highest-need schools, PreK through high school
- **Black Hair Care Drive** — led by Identity Unboxed and the Black Roots Coalition, hosted at the Zara Jo Beauty Supply table, donated to Treehouse
- **Twilight Social** — unhurried gathering as the sky turned lavender and gold
- **Vendor Village** — fifteen Black-owned businesses and five community organizations tabling on site

## Community tables — five organizations

- Eastside for All — fiscal sponsor, a DBA of the Alliance for a Just Society (https://eastsideforall.org/)
- King County Library System — makerspace and business resources (https://kcls.org/)
- SplashForward — water safety access and swim education (https://splashforward.org/)
- The Sophia Way — shelter, safety and stability for women (https://sophiaway.org/)
- Washington Saves — retirement savings program for every Washington worker (https://washingtonsaves.org/)

## Context

Held during National Black Business Month in August. Part of a pilot program within Bellevue's Diversity Advantage Initiative, anchored in the Diversity Advantage Plan 2025–2035. One of twenty-seven Bellevue-based organizations producing more than seventy cross-cultural events citywide in 2026 through the program.
